Commands spread by an airborne virus

props: Crystals that release a mist when broken, setting off Terrigenesis: people with Inhuman genes are cocooned and come out with powers.
Ordinary humans exposed to it turn to stone or die.
cont: Jiaying's Inhumans kept the crystals at Afterlife, their hidden sanctuary, to transform their own people.

origin: Asgardian (the jewel of Odin's treasure room)
Asgardian (the jewel of Odin's treasure room); holds the Space Stone
props: Its energy powers weapons and engines.
cont: S.H.I.E.L.D. kept it for decades, from Camp Lehigh to Fury's research facility.
Asgard locked it in Odin's vault.
The TVA confiscated a variant's cube.

origin: Its gem holds the Mind Stone, an Infinity Stone
props: Its blue gem holds the Mind Stone.
A touch of its tip to the chest takes over a mind, and it fires energy blasts.
HYDRA used it to give test subjects powers.
cont: S.H.I.E.L.D. took it after the Battle of New York, where HYDRA agents inside it kept it for experiments.
The Avengers then held it after Sokovia.
Valentina displays it at her gala in Washington, D.C.

origin: Older than the universe; the Reality Stone, an Infinity Stone
props: A fluid, red mist that can enter and take over a living host.
As the Reality Stone, it can turn matter into dark matter and bend reality into illusions.
cont: Bor's Asgardians hid it on a world no one could reach.
Later Sif and Volstagg left it with the Collector, who kept it on display in his museum on Knowhere.

origin: Infinity Stone (the Power Stone), from before the universe
props: A metal sphere that seals in the purple Power Stone.
Any ordinary being who touches the bare stone is destroyed, and its power can wipe out a planet.
cont: After Ronan's defeat the Guardians handed it to the Nova Corps, who locked it in a vault on Xandar.

props: An amulet that holds the Time Stone, letting its wearer turn time back, freeze it or trap it in a loop.
Even empty, its light can reveal hidden things.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
cont: The Masters of the Mystic Arts guarded it at Kamar-Taj, where the Ancient One kept the Time Stone.

props: A golden gauntlet made to hold all six Infinity Stones and channel their combined power.
With it, one snap wipes out half of all life.

origin: Built by Tony Stark, Bruce Banner and Rocket
props: A Stark nanotech gauntlet built to hold all six Infinity Stones.
Bruce uses it to bring back everyone lost in the Snap.
Only the worthy can lift it.
It returns to the hand that threw it, calls lightning and lets its wielder fly.
cont: S.H.I.E.L.D. walled it in where it fell in New Mexico; no one could lift it.
quote: Whosoever holds this hammer, if he be worthy, shall possess the power of Thor.

props: An Uru axe-hammer with a handle grown by Groot.
It calls lightning, returns when thrown and can summon the Bifrost.
A round, nearly indestructible vibranium shield that absorbs impacts.
When thrown, it ricochets and comes back.
cont: The Smithsonian displayed it after Sam gave it up, until the U.S. government handed it to John Walker.
The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
alsoHeld: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

props: A high-tension compound bow, which Clint fires with near-perfect aim.
It's matched with a quiver of specialized trick arrows.
Arrows with special heads: explosive, taser, pulse, flare, grappling cable.
Pym Particle tips shrink or grow things.
Wrist gauntlets that deliver electric shocks on contact.
They can also fire or plant stun discs from a distance.

origin: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
props: A pair of handheld quad-barrel energy blasters that fire plasma bolts.
Quill often fires them two at a time.
A powered suit of armor that flies, fires repulsor blasts and missiles, and runs on an arc reactor.
Later models flow out of a nanotech housing.

origin: Built by Tony Stark and Ho Yinsen in a Ten Rings cave
props: A bulky, crude iron suit powered by Tony's first arc reactor.
It carries flamethrowers and has a short-burst rocket for flight.
cont: The Ten Rings gathered its wreckage from the desert, and Raza handed it to Obadiah Stane, who copied the design.

origin: Stark prototype, weaponized by Hammer Industries
props: A gunmetal Stark suit of armor fitted with heavy weapons, including a shoulder-mounted gun.
It flies like Iron Man's armor.
A giant, heavily armored suit built to restrain the Hulk.
Its orbital module, Veronica, drops it in and sends replacement parts mid-fight.
A red, white and blue combat uniform with a star on the chest.
A jet-powered wingpack that lets its wearer fly and maneuver at high speed.
Later versions add guns and the Redwing drone.

origin: HYDRA (Winter Soldier program); later Wakandan vibranium
props: A cybernetic arm of great strength.
The first is metal with a red star.
A vibranium-weave suit with retractable claws.
Shuri's nanotech version forms from a necklace and absorbs kinetic energy to release it as a blast.

origin: Stark Industries; later homemade by Peter Parker
props: Tony's suits carry an AI (Karen), adjustable lenses, web-wings and many web settings.
After the spell, Peter makes his own suits, sewn by hand.
Later, they are built and repaired with a homemade Fabricator.
A red-and-gold nanotech suit that forms around Peter, with four mechanical spider legs and an 'instant kill' mode.
A suit and helmet that use Pym Particles to shrink its wearer to insect size, keeping full strength.
The suit can also grow its wearer to giant size.
The helmet lets the wearer talk to and command ants.
A Kree Starforce uniform that changes its colors on command, with a helmet that forms over her head.
Golden armor that Thanos wears into battle.
It comes with a crested helmet.

origin: Stark Industries (Tony's miniature version, built in a Ten Rings cave)
props: A miniature arc reactor in Tony's chest that keeps shrapnel from his heart and powers his armor.
Its palladium core poisons him until he builds a new element.
quote: Proof that Tony Stark has a heart

origin: Peter Parker's homemade design; later Stark-built
props: Wrist devices that fire synthetic web fluid in many settings, from lines and nets to ricochet and taser webs.
Alien energy rifles, flying chariots and huge armored Leviathans.
Salvaged parts power weapons that can blast through walls.
cont: S.H.I.E.L.D. locked a virus-carrying helmet in its Sandbox lab.
The Avengers seized Chitauri gear at Strucker's base.
Valentina displays relics at her gala in Washington, D.C.

origin: Relic of the Masters of the Mystic Arts (New York Sanctum)
props: A sentient red cloak that chooses its wearer.
It lets him levitate and fly, and it fights on its own.
A two-finger ring that lets a trained sorcerer open portals to other places by tracing a circle in the air.
A glowing blue casket that unleashes ice and bitter cold, enough to freeze a world.
It is the source of the Frost Giants' power.
cont: Odin locked it in his vault in Asgard.

props: Particles that shrink or enlarge people and objects by changing the distance between their atoms.
Shrinking far enough reaches the Quantum Realm.
A rare, nearly indestructible metal that absorbs vibrations and kinetic energy.
A glowing purple herb that gives the Black Panther enhanced strength, speed and senses.
Taking it also sends the drinker to the ancestral plane.
cont: Wakanda tended the herb in a sacred garden, kept for the Black Panther's ritual.

props: A flying aircraft carrier held aloft by four giant rotors.
Reflective panels can make it invisible.
cont: Coulson's S.H.I.E.L.D. kept one of Fury's old carriers hidden and refitted it under the Theta Protocol.

props: A vertical-takeoff jet with a stealth cloak, used to carry agents and Avengers on missions.
A small orange-and-blue spaceship that serves as Quill's home and the Guardians' transport.
The Guardians' larger spaceship, which replaces the Milano.
A cassette mixtape of 1960s and ’70s pop songs Peter's mother made him, played on his Walkman.
A pocket compass Steve keeps with a photo of Peggy Carter in its lid.
A legal agreement, ratified by 117 countries, that puts enhanced people and the Avengers under a U.N. panel's control.
Under it, registered Inhumans must wear tracking bracelets.
A handheld TVA device that opens time doors to other places and times.
It runs out of power and needs charging.
TVA devices that wipe out a branched timeline when set off.
Planted across the Sacred Timeline, they instead branch it.

origin: Copied from spells carved at Mount Wundagore
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
props: An ancient book of dark magic, the Book of the Damned, that corrupts whoever reads it.
Its spells include dreamwalking into other universes.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
cont: S.H.I.E.L.D. hid the book away, at last in the Koenigs' Labyrinth, before Ghost Rider carried it off through a portal.

props: Ten metal rings worn on the forearms that give their wielder immense power and long life.
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
They fly, strike and fire energy at their bearer's command.
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
A cursed black sword that lets its wielder kill gods and summon shadow monsters.
It slowly corrupts and kills its bearer.
A gold bangle that unlocks its wearer's latent powers, letting Kamala make hard-light constructs.
It is one of a pair of Quantum Bands; with the other, Dar-Benn tears open jump points.
A silver board the Silver Surfer rides through space and across Earth at tremendous speed.
Batons that holster on Daredevil's suit and split into two clubs or join into one.
A steel cable inside lets him swing and grapple.
An armored red bodysuit with a horned cowl, built to turn knives and blunt blows.
A bulletproof tactical vest with a white skull painted on the front.
The strongest metal on Earth, from a meteorite that struck Wakanda.
It absorbs vibrations and powers all of Wakanda's technology.
cont: Wakanda hides its vibranium behind its cloaked border.
Its Hatut Zeraze spies recover pieces taken from the kingdom.

ab: Absorbs life force and memories by touch
Adamantium claws in hands and feet
Absorbs powers and memories by touch
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

ab: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Magic through the Staff of One
Moving his mind into new bodies

props: Giant robots that hunt and capture mutants.
Bastion later turns humans into Prime Sentinels.

ab: Power Cosmic from the Surfer's board
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

idx: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
ab: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

props: A virus that turns its victims into flesh-eating zombies who keep their powers.
It spreads by eating infected flesh.
Set in the Infinity Gauntlet, a snap could reshape life everywhere.
The Mind Stone can reverse the zombie virus.
Destroyed in Wakanda's vibranium core, their energy lives on and can be absorbed by a host.

origin: Mutant bone, laced with Weapon X adamantium
props: Three retractable claws per hand that spring from Logan's knuckles.
Once bonded with adamantium they are virtually indestructible.
By 2029 the metal is slowly poisoning him.
Military dog tags bearing the name Wolverine, the only clue to his past after his memory is wiped.

origin: Built by Hank McCoy at the CIA
props: A machine that amplifies a telepath's power so the wearer of its helmet can find mutants anywhere in the world.
Sabotaged, it can harm the user.
Hijacked, it can control the user.
A helmet that blocks telepaths, so Charles cannot read or control its wearer's mind.

origin: Hank McCoy, derived from Raven's DNA
props: Meant to hide a mutation's physical signs, it backfired on Hank and turned him blue and furry.
The 1973 version keeps Hank looking human and lets Charles walk, but blocks Charles's telepathy.
A supersonic jet that takes off vertically from beneath the school grounds.
By 2023 a stealth version is in use.
It can reach orbit, as it does for the Endeavour rescue.
Ruby quartz glasses and a visor that hold back Scott's optic blasts.
Without them his eyes fire uncontrollably.
The 2023 models, built with Mystique's DNA, adapt to any mutant power.
cont: After Raven spared Trask, the U.S. government shut the Sentinel program down.

props: Two katanas Wade wears crossed on his back, his signature weapons.
A red suit and mask so his enemies can't see him bleed; it hides his scarred face.
A wrist-mounted device that sends its wearer through time.
Once repaired Wade uses it to jump between universes.
Indestructible adamantium bonded to Wolverine's skeleton and his retractable claws, strong enough to cut through almost anything.
A computer that amplifies a telepath's power to find mutants and read or alter minds, including wiping a memory.
A giant robot that builds Sentinels, which turns on its makers; its head survives and later tries to rebuild itself.
A supersonic jet; Beast later fits it with Shi'ar shield and cloaking technology.
Magneto's red helmet, worn with his costume.
Gambit charges them with kinetic energy so they explode on impact.
An orbiting asteroid base Magneto made as a haven for mutants.
It can be steered or dropped toward Earth.
Its computer can send people through time, and through it Rogue speaks with Eson.
A trap in its hilt springs blades into the hand of anyone who grabs it without disarming it first.
A folding throwing blade that spins through vampires and flies back to Blade's hand.
A serum that holds back Blade's vampire thirst for blood, though it is losing its effect.
It can also tame a newly turned vampire's hunger.
A pair of sai, three-pronged daggers that Elektra fights with and throws.

origin: Taken from a magic academy's vault by Tina Minoru
props: A retractable magic staff that channels its wielder's power for spells, such as tracking someone.
Its power can overwhelm the user.
Nico can summon it even after it has been broken.
Weaponized gauntlets worn over the fists that fire powerful blasts.
A spacecraft that could take Jonah home.
The new one his family builds needs all four of them to power it.
A green performance-enhancing gas that greatly boosts strength and agility but drives its user to madness.
An armored green flight suit with a mask, built for soldiers; it protects the wearer in combat.
A one-person jet glider with a blade at its front and remote-controlled flight.
Pumpkin-shaped grenades, some of which burn victims to skeletons.
A red and blue suit with raised black webbing and a full mask that hides his identity.
An inhibitor chip stops the AI from controlling Otto's mind.
Later, Stark nanotech fuses to them.
cont: Doctor Strange locked Otto and his arms in a cell beneath the Sanctum.

props: Genetically modified spiders whose bite gave Peter his powers.
Their extracted venom twists Harry into a goblin.
cont: Oscorp kept the spiders in a restricted lab.
Later it drained their venom and destroyed them.

origin: Built by Peter Parker, with Oscorp's web formula
props: Wrist-mounted mechanical shooters that fire strong web lines.
Electro can short them out until they are magnetized.
A spandex suit and full mask that hide Peter's identity, first with yellow-tinted lenses.
A later suit has large white lenses.
A super collider that opens portals to other universes.
Its tests pulled Spider-People into Miles's world.
Its blast turned a scientist into the Spot.
Its bite gave Miles spider powers, including camouflage and a venom strike.

origin: Peter Parker's spare suit, painted by Miles
props: A black suit Miles paints with red webbing, worn with web-shooters.
A giant robot Peni pilots through a psychic link with the spider that lives inside it.

origin: Miguel O'Hara and his AI Lyla
props: Wrist watches that open portals for jumping between universes.
Miguel can track them and switch them off remotely.
Forced onto Cassandra Nova, it cuts her off from her powers.
